scope: Ticket 23 stage one, part two: the capacity-limited replay package with three sampling policies, two eviction policies, a declared privacy policy, a serializable state that resumes the same sample sequence, and the NoReplay control. The replay store is persisted as an optional part of checkpoint.State.
environment: uptime at the start of the recorded run: 19:18 up 11 days, 57 mins, load averages 6.39 4.98 4.07 (a shared machine; two other agents were building and testing the same repository during this run, so wall times in test.log are not timing measurements)
no external data, no network, no data/ input: every fixture is built in the test
input_fingerprints: replay/policy.go, replay/store.go, replay/sampling.go and replay/replay_test.go (the package and its tests, created by this work)
generator: math/rand/v2 rand.New(rand.NewPCG(7, 0)), the same convention simulate's null models declare as "pcg"
every hand computation below uses capacity 4 and seed 7
observed_result: Bounded values are drawn by rejection on whole uint64 draws (a value at or above the largest multiple of the bound that fits in a uint64 is discarded), so the draw count alone reproduces the stream position; none of the values below was rejected. FIFO: adding steps 1..6 to a capacity of 4 keeps [3 4 5 6], has seen 6 and has drawn 0, because the oldest item leaving is not a random decision. Reservoir: adding steps 1..10 fills the four slots, then draws one value per further item and keeps it when that value modulo the number seen lands inside the capacity: e5 seen 5, 4971928291090985182 % 5 = 2, slot 2; e6 seen 6, 5528821527542695328 % 6 = 2, slot 2; e7 seen 7, 2134937714366092113 % 7 = 2, slot 2; e8 seen 8, 3091447866230484581 % 8 = 5, dropped; e9 seen 9, 15963695826586302654 % 9 = 0, slot 0; e10 seen 10, 14648062316321977721 % 10 = 1, slot 1. Expected and observed final contents [9 10 7 4], seen 10, draws 6. Uniform sampling settles the whole order with a Fisher-Yates pass (position i swaps with i + draw % (len - i)): over four items i=0 gives 4971928291090985182 % 4 = 2 -> [2 1 0 3], i=1 gives 5528821527542695328 % 3 = 2 -> [2 3 0 1], i=2 gives 2134937714366092113 % 2 = 1 -> [2 3 1 0]; Sample(2) returns steps [3 4] with 3 draws, PerTask {a:2} and no bucket report. Task-balanced sampling over steps 1,2,4 of task a and step 3 of task b shuffles task a with 4971928291090985182 % 3 = 1 and 5528821527542695328 % 2 = 0 into the order 2,1,4, needs no draw for the single item of task b, and round robins: Sample(4) returns [2 3 1 4] with PerTask {a:3, b:1} and 2 draws; Sample(2) returns [2 3] with PerTask {a:1, b:1}. Time-balanced sampling over steps 10,20,30,40 makes ceil(sqrt(4)) = 2 equal-count buckets over the step order, shuffles each with 4971928291090985182 % 2 = 0 and 5528821527542695328 % 2 = 0 (both leave the bucket alone) and round robins: Sample(4) returns [10 30 20 40] with PerBucket [2 2] and 2 draws; Sample(2) returns [10 30] with PerBucket [1 1]. Every policy samples without replacement: a request of 9 against 4 stored items returns all four exactly once and Duplicates is 0 in every case, measured by checking the returned slot indices rather than assumed. Sample(0) is refused; an empty store returns nothing, draws nothing and is not an error. Contamination barrier: Add refuses the test split, an unknown split such as "tes", an empty split, an empty task id, a negative or NaN weight, a missing, empty, ragged or non-finite input or target, and a caller-supplied fingerprint or raw flag, under both eviction policies, and a refused experience leaves the items, the seen count and the draw count untouched. Privacy: with StoreRaw false the sampled items carry Raw false, no arrays and two SHA-256 fingerprints, one of which equals the independently recomputed row-major hash; with StoreRaw true the same fingerprint is present alongside the arrays. Retention drop_after_sample removes the two sampled items and leaves the other two, keep_until_evicted leaves all of them. New refuses a zero or negative capacity and an unknown or empty sampling, eviction or retention policy. Snapshot and resume: two identical runs sample identically, a snapshot taken between samples survives a JSON round trip, RestoreSnapshot rebuilds a store whose own snapshot is deep-equal to it, and three further rounds of add-then-sample on the resumed store return the same steps with the same draw counts as the uninterrupted store, ending in an identical state. Restore refuses an unknown state schema, a state holding more items than it has seen, a state over the capacity, a test split inside the items and an item whose raw flag contradicts the store's privacy policy. The control: NoReplay accepts a legal experience and keeps nothing, refuses held-out data, returns an empty sample with zero draws, reports Replayed false and keeps an empty state, while a real store reports Replayed true; Report names the capacity, sampling, eviction, retention, raw storage, seed and generator in one comparable value. Checkpoint: a run without a replay store writes no "replay" key anywhere in the document and loads with a nil replay part, a run with one round trips the declaration and the reached state bit for bit and the loaded part resumes to the same next sample as the original, and a hand-edited part missing the buffer, missing the state, empty, or carrying an unknown sampling, eviction, retention or state schema, or a test split inside its items, is refused.
assumption_statement: This is a software-contract result on hand-sized fixtures, not a learning result. The capacity is 4 and the seed is 7 everywhere, so the expected sequences could be derived by hand from the pinned PCG stream; that derivation was done with a throwaway program that uses only math/rand/v2, not this package, and the pinned numbers are checked against the generator in the test itself. The bucket rule of the time-balanced policy is a declared engineering choice: ceil(sqrt(n)) buckets of as equal a count as the item count allows, over the items ordered by Step with ties in insertion order, rather than equal step ranges, so a burst of experience at one moment cannot fill a bucket that then dominates every sample. Whole-order shuffling is likewise declared: the number of draws a Sample takes depends only on what the store holds and how the policy groups it, never on the requested size, which is what makes a snapshot between two samples enough to continue the sequence. The reservoir policy gives a uniform sample of everything seen only under the keep_until_evicted retention policy; combined with drop_after_sample the privacy rule wins and that guarantee no longer holds, which the package documents and Report makes visible by naming both policies.

limitations: Fixture scale only: capacity 4 and at most ten experiences, each a one or two row matrix. No large buffer, no memory accounting and no throughput measurement.
One platform: macOS arm64, go1.26.5. No Ubuntu or Windows run.
Teacher sources are not implemented (ticket 27). Nothing here stores or replays a teacher response.

Adaptive evaluation is stage two of this ticket (LRN-10). The scoring split is a declared name the store accepts; the counted refusal of scoring-split experiences belongs to the contamination check of that stage, and only the test split is refused here.

The replay state is an optional part of checkpoint.State, not of learning.TrainingSnapshot as the ticket contract wrote it. The trainer owns no store, so a TrainingSnapshot field would have been written by nobody and lost on every Snapshot; the deviation is recorded in the ticket.

Statistical properties are not measured. The reservoir is Algorithm R and the shuffles are Fisher-Yates over an unbiased bounded draw, but no test estimates the resulting distribution over many runs; the tests pin the exact sequence one declared seed produces.
Concurrency is covered only by the race detector over single-goroutine tests; no test drives one store from several goroutines.
